Black & McDonald is an integrated, multi trade service provider that safely delivers high quality construction, facilities management, and technical solutions. We are a family-owned and family-run company that employs thousands of highly skilled and talented professionals across North America. With 100+ years of diverse market experience, we are a forward thinking organization with a strong track record of delivering operational excellence and customer-focused solutions that stand the test of time.
  
  
**About This Career Opportunity**
Black & McDonald Limited is seeking a Maintenance Mechanic at our location in Ottawa, Ontario. The Maintenance Mechanic will maintain, troubleshoot, and repair various mechanical and plumbing devices and systems to achieve optimum life span of equipment in a National Museum.
  
  
**Duties & Responsabilities**
Work shall include but not necessarily be limited to the following:
  
  

* Perform shift tours and log readings
* Start up / shut down major building equipment
* All water treatment duties
* Diesel, fire alarm, life safety tests
* Perform minor repairs
* Major fan and AHU maintenance and alignment
* Minor chiller and heat pump servicing and troubleshooting
* Compressor maintenance
* All mechanical maintenance duties such as filter and belt changing
* Carry out preventative maintenance tasks as requested by the CMMS system
* Respond to the Client’s “trouble call system” as necessary and carry out appropriate repairs
* Verify the quality of work completed by various subcontractors
* Report to the Project Manager on the day-to-day operations of this function of the contract

**Skills, Abilities & Other Requirements**

* Extensive experience with HVAC and mechanical systems and/or an Ontario trade of Qualifications or equivalent.

**Due to contractual requirements, candidates must be able to obtain and maintain a Reliability clearance (must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident of 5 years).**
*This position’s wage rate follows the 787 Union Agreement schedule.*
Black & McDonald welcomes and encourages applications from persons with accessibility accommodation requirements. Accessibility accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruitment and selection process.
  
  
If you are an existing Black & McDonald employee, please notify your supervisor of your interest and intent to apply before applying.

Job Description

Western EcoSystems Technology (WEST), founded in 1990, has grown to be one of the premier environmental and statistical consulting firms in the United States. In 2017, WEST expanded into Canada by opening an office in Calgary, AB, with staff now in Alberta, Saskatchewan, Quebec, Ontario, and New Brunswick. In our continued drive to provide outstanding professional consulting services and original solutions to a wide range of natural resource problems, we are looking for an energetic and experienced **Ecological Field Technician** to join our team.

  

**Number of positions available:** 1

**Positions Type:** Temporary/Full Time

**Location:** Calgary, AB, remote in Alberta

**Tentative Start Date:** November 1, 2026

**Job Closing:** Until filled

**Wage Range:** $21.63 - $27.88/hour CAD

**Benefits:** WEST Benefits

  

**Job Description:**  
Primary duties may include:

  

* Assist with wetland and watercourse field surveys and desktop assessments.
* Assist with soil and vegetation field surveys.
* Assist with wildlife field surveys (e.g., amphibian surveys).
* Assist in reporting (including, but not limited to: Wetland Assessment Impact Reports, Conservation & Reclamation Plans (C&Rs), Mitigation Plans, Environmental Protection Plans (EPPs), PDSAs and Site Restoration, and Soil Management Plans.
* Assisting with completion of data recording, quality control, and GIS mapping.
* Promote WEST’s core values of quality client service and a collaborative team approach while maintaining a positive and respectful work atmosphere.
  

This position consists of approximately 10% office-based work and 90% field-based work (fieldwork occurring year-round), and travel between the field and the Calgary office. Fieldwork will require long days (8-12 hours), in a range of temperature extremes and wind speeds. Candidates must be comfortable with hazards typical of rural environments (e.g., driving a four-wheel drive vehicle, dust, mud, snow, extreme heat, cold, working around cattle). Candidates must promote WEST’s core values of quality client service and a collaborative team approach while maintaining a positive and respectful work atmosphere. Fieldwork can also occur in remote locations, which will require candidates to be comfortable and able to work and operate vehicles in rugged, steep terrain within areas with large carnivores. The position may require international field work; the candidate must be comfortable and willing to work internationally. Lastly, fieldwork can occur in areas with little to no cellphone signal. Candidates must be comfortable using satellite and radio devices for regular communication.

  

Staff may work independently or in small crews and must be able to communicate and coordinate effectively with site management and WEST supervisors.

  

*This is a general description of the functions for this position and is not inclusive of all the duties that may be associated with this position.*

Job Requirements

**Work Location Requirements:**

This position will involve work in both Canada and the United States. The successful candidate is expected to perform approximately **85% of their work in Canada and 15% in the United States**, although actual percentages may vary based on business needs and project requirements. Candidates must be legally authorized to work and travel in both countries as required. This role may require compliance with applicable immigration, tax, payroll, and employment regulations in each jurisdiction.

  

Employment is contingent upon the employee maintaining all necessary work authorization, social security number (SSN), travel documentation, and eligibility requirements needed to perform work assignments in both Canada and the United States.

  

**Job Requirements:**

* Legally allowed to work in Canada (i.e., Canadian citizen, Canadian permanent resident, or have an existing VISA with no work restrictions) Please note: US citizens require a Canadian work visa to work in Canada.
* A valid passport and ability to obtain a TN Visa in the USA.
* Completion of a bachelor’s degree in biological sciences, environmental sciences, or a related discipline.
* Possession of a valid driver’s licence with no restrictions.
* Able to obtain a driver’s abstract that meets WEST’s minimum criteria to operate a motor vehicle on behalf of the company.
* Ability to rent a vehicle from a rental agency (e.g., Enterprise).
* Competence in Microsoft Office (advanced knowledge of Word and Excel), ArcGIS/QGIS
* Ability to work long days (up to 12 hours) in the field and sometimes long shifts (up to 24 days) and lift up to 25 lbs.
* Ability to hike in rugged, steep terrain for extended periods of time.
* Capacity to work independently and interact positively with project managers, supervisors, clients, field partners, and landowners.
* Excellent time management and organizational skills.
* Ability to work well under time constraints and meet deliverable targets and deadlines.
* High level of initiative and ability to think critically to solve challenging problems.
* Highly developed ability to follow protocols and work efficiently in the field and office.
* Capable of adhering to all health and safety requirements outlined by WEST and our clients, for the duration of their employment.
  

**Desired Skills:**

* A completed diploma or bachelor’s degree or higher in biological sciences, environmental sciences, or a related discipline and at least 1 year of relevant experience in wetlands, soil or vegetation.
* In the process of attaining a professional designation applicable for conducting professional sign off in Alberta or eligible for registration (e.g., P.Ag or P.Biol.).
* Experience conducting wetland and watercourse field surveys
* Experience with identifying vegetation or conducting vegetation surveys
* Experience conducting soil assessments or surveys
* Experience with wildlife surveys
* Experience with construction or environmental monitoring.
* Experience using GIS software (e.g., QGIS or ArcGIS).
* Previous experience using tablet data collection systems and apps (e.g., Fulcrum, Field Maps, and/or Survey123).
  

*Successful candidates must be able to provide a driver’s abstract that meets WEST’s minimum criteria to operate a motor vehicle on behalf of the company. Successful candidates must also be able to pass a drug and alcohol test that meets the minimum criteria of WEST and our clients. Candidates must be capable of adhering to all health and safety requirements, outlined by WEST and our clients, for the duration of their employment.*

items.title: Field Service Engineer - Canada
items.job_description:
**Job Description:**
Founded in 1904, ESAB Corporation is a premier narrowly diversified global leader in connected fabrication technology and gas control solutions. Our rich history of innovative products, workflow solutions, and business system, ESAB Business Excellence, enables our purpose of Shaping the World We Imagine™. We’re looking to hire a talented Field Service Engineer based in Canada (remote / field-based with regional and national travel).
  
  
**Position Overview & Technical Impact**
ESAB is seeking a high-caliber, solutions-driven Field Service Engineer (FSE) to lead technical commissioning, system diagnostics, preventive maintenance, and lifecycle support for our industry-leading automated cutting systems across Canada. In this role, you will serve as the frontline technical authority for high-precision CNC cutting tables, multi-axis gantry systems, advanced plasma power sources, oxy-fuel stations, and integrated digital cutting automation.
  
  
Working directly at customer manufacturing facilities, heavy fabrication plants, shipyards, and structural steel operations, you will solve complex electromechanical, drive, and software challenges, optimize cutting cycle performance, and partner with plant engineering teams to maximize equipment uptime. If you thrive on troubleshooting complex industrial systems, working autonomously in the field, and delivering engineering excellence, this role offers direct technical impact and clear pathways for career progression within ESAB.
  
  
Key Technical Responsibilities
  
  

* Advanced Diagnostics & Root-Cause Troubleshooting: Perform comprehensive electromechanical, electronic, and pneumatic diagnostics on automated CNC cutting machines, AC/DC servo drive systems, height sensors, and high-frequency plasma units using oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, schematic drawings, and diagnostic software.
* Installation & Turnkey Commissioning: Lead on-site system integration, machine alignment, leveling, I/O verification, CNC parameter configuration, process gas calibration, and test cutting to ensure systems meet factory specifications and customer acceptance criteria.
* Preventative & Corrective Maintenance: Execute planned multi-point maintenance audits, component rebuilds, motion calibration, torch consumable optimization, and emergency repair interventions to ensure 99%+ operational reliability.
* Control Systems & Automation Support: Diagnose and interface with CNC controllers (e.g., Vision, Columbus CAD/CAM interfaces), PLC logic, industrial fieldbuses (Ethernet/IP, Modbus, PROFINET), and safety interlocks (CSA Z432 / ISO 13849 / NFPA 79 standards).
* Client Enablement & Operational Training: Deliver technical training for customer maintenance technicians, CNC programmers, and operators on machine safety, daily operation, torch setup, and first-line preventive care.
* Engineering Feedback & Field Reporting: Author detailed Field Service Reports (FSRs) documenting failure modes, root causes, corrective actions, and recommended preventative spares. Collaborate with Aftermarket and R&D engineering teams to drive design reliability improvements.
* Spare Parts & Aftermarket Advisory: Assess system wear profiles, formulate bill-of-materials (BOM) recommendations for critical spare parts packages, and support customer retrofit/upgrade roadmaps.

**Qualifications & Requirements**
**Required Qualifications**

* Education & Technical Training: College Diploma or Advanced Diploma in Electrical / Electronic Engineering Technology (EET), Mechatronics, Industrial Automation, Electromechanical / Mechanical Engineering
* Technology, or equivalent technical trade certificate / Red Seal endorsement (e.g., 442A / 433A / 309A), or Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) technical qualification.
* Field Experience: 2–5+ years of hands-on experience in industrial field service, machine tool repair, robotics, or automated manufacturing systems.
* Electromechanical Acumen: Proven ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, ladder logic, hydraulic/pneumatic schematics, and mechanical assembly blueprints.
* Safety & Standards: Demonstrated commitment to industrial safety standards (Canadian OH&S compliance, WHMIS, Lockout/Tagout [LOTO], CSA Z462 / NFPA 70E Arc Flash awareness).
* Physical Requirements: Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. (23 kg) unassisted, work in industrial plant environments, climb ladders, maneuver around large gantry machinery, and stand/walk for extended periods during commissioning.
* Mobility & Driving: Valid Canadian Driver’s License with a clean driving record and a valid Canadian Passport (or eligibility to obtain one) for occasional cross-border travel/training in the U.S.

**Preferred Qualifications & Skills**

* Industry Exposure: Direct experience with thermal cutting technologies (high-definition plasma, oxy-fuel, fiber laser, or waterjet) and CNC motion platforms.
* Software / CAD/CAM: Familiarity with CNC nesting software, CAD/CAM file formats (DXF, DWG, ESSI, G-code), and remote diagnostic tools.
* Bilingual Capability: Bilingual proficiency in English and French (verbal and written) is a strong asset; Spanish proficiency is also valued to support collaborative North American engineering initiatives.

Work Environment, Travel & Total Rewards
  
  

* Work Environment: High-paced industrial manufacturing, steel fabrication, shipbuilding, and energy sector job sites. Full PPE and strict adherence to plant safety protocols required.
* Travel Scope: Up to 100% regional and domestic travel across Canada to customer facilities, with occasional cross-border travel to the U.S. for advanced training and technical support; comprehensive travel expense coverage provided.

**Description**
The
**Maintenance-Life Safety**
within the
**Facilities Management**
is currently seeking a Full-time Regular
**Life Safety Technician.**
Facilities Management is responsible for providing the operations and capital asset management functions for the University. Operations includes all activities associated with the routine, day to day use, support and maintenance of buildings or physical assets; inclusive of administration, management fees, normal/routine maintenance, custodial services and cleaning, fire protection services, pest control, snow removal, grounds care, landscaping, environmental operations and record keeping, trash-recycle removal, service contracts, leases and utility charges (electric, gas/oil, water). Capital asset management is the identification and prioritization of facility and infrastructure physical, functional, and budgetary needs, spanning a multi-year timeframe. It also includes the process of reinvesting funds into physical assets in support of the organizational mission, above and beyond normal routine operations and maintenance.
  
  
The Operations & Maintenance work unit of Facilities Management is responsible to ensure that building structures, utility distribution systems, building operating and monitoring systems for the university owned and leased properties are operated and maintained in a reliable, efficient and cost effective manner to ensure a safe and comfortable work environment in which campus users can carry out their activities.
  
  
This position reports to the Manager, Maintenance and Contracting. This position is a part of the AUPE Collective Bargaining Unit. The normal shift is 7.5 hours per day, five days per week, usually Monday to Friday, however, transfer to other shifts, with notice, is a possibility. Overtime may be required, and the incumbent will be expected to participate in a rotating "on-call or stand-by" schedule. Callouts to the campus can be expected during emergencies.
  
  
This position requires work be carried out with the following conditions: within confined spaces, scaffolds, and lifts of heights up to 4 metres, heavy lifting, year round indoor and outdoor responsibilities and controlled hazardous environments.
  
  
This position is highly analytical in project planning, system and event documentation and working with contract personnel required to complete all code required inspections, repairs, verifications and installations. Work is highly complex and stressful. Life Safety Systems Technician must resolve complex problems where there is little or no documentation. Impact of error when dealing with University Life Safety Systems is severe. Systems at the University vary from state of the art, CPU based, fully programmable fire and gas detection systems to systems that are obsolete but must be maintained in peak operating condition. Individuals in this group coordinate and assist emergency personnel responding to disasters campus wide. The level of responsibility is very high as even a minute error or omission could lead to loss of life and extreme liability for the University.
  
  
**Primary Purpose of the Position**
(key purpose, functions, roles):
  
  
The Life Safety Systems Department is responsible for the primary life safety systems: fire alarm control panels on the campus-wide control network. The systems typically include detection, communication and signaling devices, sprinklers, preaction systems, deluge systems, standpipe fire fighting systems, fire pumps, fire hydrants, fire hoses, fire extinguishers, chemical fire suppression systems (halon, inergen, CO), kitchen fire suppression systems (dry and wet chemical), hazardous fume and gas detection systems, building emergency control devices as well as other peripherals. Duties include:
  
  

* Ensuring that all Life Safety Systems are operational at all times, as down time is not acceptable.
* Maintaining and operating all building safety systems and related equipment campus wide.
* Proper design, installation, verification, maintenance and operation of Life Safety systems including sprinklers, fire alarms, fire standpipes, fire pumps, fire hydrants, fire hoses, fire extinguishers, kitchen hood suppression systems, special hazards suppression systems and hazardous gas detection systems on campus along with associated University controlled buildings.
* Design and implementation of: programming, inspection, verification, calibration, modification, troubleshooting, repair and documentation of all life safety systems on campus, as well as identification and immediate correction of Life Safety concerns within the University.
* Orientation, coordination, and mentoring of contractors ensuring that all related code requirements are met, verification and approval of work done by contractors and University personnel working on life safety systems; computer programming of Life Safety Systems.
* Coordination and overseeing of work done by various contractors and specialists who may be working on campus systems due to insurance requirements or on projects such as renovations or new construction.
* Giving advice to representatives of system manufacturers, suppliers and contractors who are generally here with little knowledge of the systems on campus and university protocols and procedures.
* Running diagnostics on systems using laptops; inspection, testing and verification of systems.
* Troubleshooting and repair of systems.
* Attending planning meetings.
* Ensuring codes and University procedures and standards are adhered to.
* Reviewing and approval of plans and blue prints for new installations and retrofits.
* Training of campus personnel and the University of Calgary projects teams on system operations and effect.
* Responding to emergencies on campus to direct personnel and ascertain problems.
* Supply of technical information, advice, guidance and/or training to University departments such as Safety, Security, Facilities Management and Development, Risk Management, engineers, manufacturers, suppliers and contractors is required.
* Ensuring compliance with NFPA Standards, Alberta Building Code, Electrical Code and University of Calgary established standards, policies and procedures.
* Acting as the U of C representative for fire alarm verifications and approvals.
* Life Safety Systems personnel contribute knowledge and experience in the areas of various electronic systems on campus as well as back-up support for the building management system.
* Communication with customers, contractors, suppliers and trade staff to successfully complete tasks.
* Completion of computerized records related to work is also required.

**Summary of Key Responsibilities**
(job functions include but are not limited to):
  
  

* Ensure other University departments as well as contractors follow safety codes and procedures during planning and completion of projects.
* Ensure University exposure to risk and liability is not adversely affected by work of self or others.
* Develops and delivers Life Safety Systems training and/or presentations on all relevant stakeholders on and off-campus.
* Ensure notification of authorities and required University departments of any adverse situations that may exist on campus.
* Develop and design, install and maintain proper programming for the smooth interfacing/ running old and new campus wide Life Safety Systems.
* Ensure all life safety systems are fully functional during and after normal working hours.
* Respond to inquiries and emergency situations after normal working hours.
* Development of the programs and processes needed to keep systems fully operational.
* Make tough decisions under stressful conditions without exposing University to undue liability.
* Plan and detail projects so the information required by others is available.
* Identify problems and create solutions for them.
* As a member of Commissioning Team, provide expertise and approval on the design of blue prints, schematics and plans across campus, ensuring systems meet or exceeds industry standards.
* Act as University liaison between emergency response crews and inspectors during normal and emergency situations.
* Required to attend in all situations involving suppression system discharge, gas detection system activation, sprinkler system activation, Life Safety equipment malfunction, Life Safety
* Systems vandalism, Life Safety Systems shutdowns, and Life Safety Systems verifications.
* Required to attend when fire alarm systems are activated.
* Ensure the work assigned or encountered is completed as required by the standards of the applicable codes and University specifications, standards and procedures.
* Manage the programming, installation, set-up, and maintenance of complex 4100U Fire Safety Systems and respond to changing technology.
* Required to become familiar with all existing University Life Safety Systems, as well as acquire knowledge of new trends, techniques, codes and equipment within the industry, as they become relevant to the operation of the University.
* Organize, analyze and process information in a logical prioritized order under any circumstances or conditions.
* Supply expert direction to others.
* Develop and mentor procedures for others who may have access to Life Safety Systems.
* Maintain records, as-built blueprints, and schematic diagrams when altering any existing or new systems.
* Ensure that equipment, workspaces, and tools supplied by the University are used for their intended purposes, are maintained in safe working order.
* Ensures the work assigned is completed as required and is in compliance with the University specifications, standards and procedures.
* Responsible to become familiar with all existing University structures and systems, as well as acquire knowledge of new trends, techniques, codes and equipment as they become relevant to the operation of the University.
* Ensures that equipment, workspaces, and tools supplied by the University are used for their intended purposes, and are maintained in a safe working order.
* Manages own time effectively and ensures immediate supervisor is kept informed of activities, and progress of work.
* Pleasantly and respectfully interacts with co-workers, supervisors, contractors, consultants, suppliers, students and other members of the University community.
* Discretion, confidentiality, and attention to detail are required attributes.
* Is expected to actively participate in own training and development in coordination with the department, and is willing to learn and adapt to change.
* Meets all ongoing OHS initiatives, follows University OHS policies, procedures and OHS Legislation as required; ensuring personal, public and co-worker safety when completing tasks or engaging in potentially hazardous situations.
* Is familiar with the University of Calgary "Statement on Principles of Conduct" and conducts himself/herself according to these Principles in all situations when acting on behalf of the University of Calgary.
* Ensures regular work attendance and timely reporting for start of shift.
* Ensures that personal hygiene, attire and grooming are appropriate for the work environment.

**Qualifications / Requirements:**

* Must have an Alberta Journeyman Electrical Certificate, preferably with Masters License, or a completed CFAA certification with several years experience in troubleshooting, repair, testing and programming of complex fire protection systems.
* An asset would be for those who possess Electronic Technician or Technologist Certification with fire alarm ticket, sprinkler certification.
* Excellent organizational and communication skills as interaction with a diverse group such as engineers, faculty, fire inspectors, fire fighters, safety inspectors, management, planning and projects groups, as well as various campus departments is expected.
* Good working knowledge of current Canadian Electrical Code, current Alberta Building and Fire Codes and pertinent NFPA Standards is required.
* Must have expertise in of computerized fire alarms, sprinkler systems, chemical suppression systems and gas detection systems.
* Must be able to analyze information and make decisions in stressful situations.
* Must be able to understand and analyze complex electrical and electronic circuit diagrams as well as building plans and specifications.
* Must be able to perform physically demanding work, and be able to work on ladders at various heights.
* Must have good manual dexterity, must be able to distinguish colors and have the ability to do exact work, as consequence of error would result in unsafe conditions for University occupants.
* Must hold a valid Class 5 driver¿s license (cannot be a graduated license) with proven good driving record (abstract required).

November 24, 2026.

**PROJECT OVERVIEW**

The Appeals Commission (the “Commission”) is an administrative tribunal established under the Workers’ Compensation Act as the final level of appeal for worker’s compensation matters in the province of Alberta. The Appeals Commission consists of four diverse divisions including a tribunal made up of adjudicators and staff; an advocate office that operates as an independent program; a medical panels program that facilitates an independent medical panel process; and a secretariat that provides administrative and operational support to all components of the organization.

Reporting to the Senior Appeals Assistant, the temporary Appeals Assistant (AA) role is the main point of contact on the day of the appeal hearing. The AA is required to provide a wide range of front line assistance to external parties to the appeal, as well as support and guidance to internal stakeholders such as Appeals Officers, Hearing Chairs, Vice Chairs and Commissioners, in matters relating to the AA role. Before the hearing, the AA is solely response for pre-hearing administration. During the hearing, the AA oversees the hearing recording, manages the parties assists the panel and the parties with additional appeal-related documents, and is expected to take the lead of parties become distressed. After the hearing, the AA is responsible for updating the appeal file, and once the decision is written, the AA is required to format, proofread and send the appeal decision for publication and distribution.

**DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES**

Key Responsibilities:
  
1. Providing efficient and accurate support to Appeals Officers
  
– Prepares and disperses Appeals Officers’ (AOs) correspondence to participating parties
  
– Creates the Document Index for the Appeal Documents Package (ADP)
  
– Informed the assigned Appeals Officer of any new submissions or circumstances occuring at the hearing (e.g. last minute submissions provided, requests for travel, changes of address, provisions of a wage loss form to the parties, etc.), following up where an adjournment occurs

2. Manages hearing communications and situational irregularities fo scheduled hearings
  
– Notifies the panel of any prehearing anomolies that might impact the success of the hearing
  
– Coordinates set up and sharing of teleconference/video conference information with the parties and the panels
  
– Instruct parties in how to participate in all formats of hearings – in person, teleconference, video
  
– Attends, records hearings hearings, troubleshoots and resolves any process or technical problems
  
– Responds to party inquiries and concerns prior to commencement of the hearing
  
– Supports clients, including when distress, emergency or crisis situations arise

3. Ensures correct statuses are maintained
  
– Enter statuses on ACES for work completed on hearing chair decisions, ADPs, and AO correspondence
  
– Ensures ACES status benchmarks are maintained to reflect timelines for assigned work from Hearing Chairs and AOs
  
– Confirms the status of an appeal with the Hearing Chair upon completion of a hearing to meet the AC decision timelines
  
– Resolves any errors or omissions of stats with IT Coordinator to ensure accurate reporting

4. Audits and prepares Hearing Chair decisions for distribution
  
– Formats and proofs policy and legislation in the draft decision document
  
– Provides plain language and other editing feedback to the Hearing Chair
  
– Ensures decisions documents re in accordance with approved Appeals Commission style guide and decision format protocol
  
– Processes errors flagged in an issues decision
  
– Communicates with Hearing Chairs regarding any suggested changes and/or apparent errors
  
– Ensures the final decision document is publication ready for uploading on CanLII for public access

**MANDATORY SKILLS**

– High School Diploma/GED. (Yes or No)
  
– Experience adapting to new business environments business and technical teams, coordinating with vendors, managing stakeholder relationships, and facilitating collaboration to achieve project objectives. (2 years+)
  
– Experience using Microsoft Office Suite tools. (2 years+)
  
– Experience working in a fast-paced role, to problem solve/troubleshoot, while working independently and in a team environments. (2 years+)
  
– Relevant experience in a role similar to this. Experience must be applicable to this role. (2 years+)
  
– Experience working with clients/stakeholders to identify, gather, document, and analyze business data and process requirements. (2 years+)

**DESIRABLE / NICE TO HAVE SKILLS**

– Relevant post-secondary education in the area of office administration. Acceptable education includes degrees, diplomas and certificates. (Yes or No)
  
– Experience with Information Governance, or records management and information management. (2 years+)
  
– Experience with information management concepts, privacy, and security issues relating to ATIA (Access to Information Act) and POPA (Protection of Privacy Act) – previously known as FOIP. (2 years+)
  
– Experience working directly within the Government of Alberta, 1GX (SAP), or a comparable Canadian public-sector ERP environment. (2 years+)
  
– Experience working with workers compensation systems (i.e. WCB). (2 years+)

**NOT FOR YOU?**

Check out our other opportunities at https://tri-global.com or follow us on LinkedIn. We thank all candidates in advance. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Before the hearing, the AA is solely response for pre-hearing administration. During the hearing, the AA oversees the hearing recording, manages the parties assists the panel and the parties with additional appeal-related documents, and is expected to take the lead of parties become distressed. After the hearing, the AA is responsible for updating the appeal file, and once the decision is written, the AA is required to format, proofread and send the appeal decision for publication and distribution.

**DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES**

Key Responsibilities:
  
1. Providing efficient and accurate support to Appeals Officers
  
– Prepares and disperses Appeals Officers’ (AOs) correspondence to participating parties
  
– Creates the Document Index for the Appeal Documents Package (ADP)
  
– Informed the assigned Appeals Officer of any new submissions or circumstances occuring at the hearing (e.g. last minute submissions provided, requests for travel, changes of address, provisions of a wage loss form to the parties, etc.), following up where an adjournment occurs

2. Manages hearing communications and situational irregularities fo scheduled hearings
  
– Notifies the panel of any prehearing anomolies that might impact the success of the hearing
  
– Coordinates set up and sharing of teleconference/video conference information with the parties and the panels
  
– Instruct parties in how to participate in all formats of hearings – in person, teleconference, video
  
– Attends, records hearings hearings, troubleshoots and resolves any process or technical problems
  
– Responds to party inquiries and concerns prior to commencement of the hearing
  
– Supports clients, including when distress, emergency or crisis situations arise

3. Ensures correct statuses are maintained
  
– Enter statuses on ACES for work completed on hearing chair decisions, ADPs, and AO correspondence
  
– Ensures ACES status benchmarks are maintained to reflect timelines for assigned work from Hearing Chairs and AOs
  
– Confirms the status of an appeal with the Hearing Chair upon completion of a hearing to meet the AC decision timelines
  
– Resolves any errors or omissions of stats with IT Coordinator to ensure accurate reporting

4. Audits and prepares Hearing Chair decisions for distribution
  
– Formats and proofs policy and legislation in the draft decision document
  
– Provides plain language and other editing feedback to the Hearing Chair
  
– Ensures decisions documents re in accordance with approved Appeals Commission style guide and decision format protocol
  
– Processes errors flagged in an issues decision
  
– Communicates with Hearing Chairs regarding any suggested changes and/or apparent errors
  
– Ensures the final decision document is publication ready for uploading on CanLII for public access

**MANDATORY SKILLS**

– High School Diploma/GED. (Yes or No)
  
– Clear verbal and written communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with a diverse group. (Yes or No)
  
– Exceptional organizational skills and ability to prioritize multiple responsibilities. The ability to work on multiple projects at one time and to prioritize tasks. (Yes or No)
  
– The ability to pay attention to detail. (Yes or No)
  
– Experience adapting to new business environments business and technical teams, coordinating with vendors, managing stakeholder relationships, and facilitating collaboration to achieve project objectives. (2 years+)
  
– Experience using Microsoft Office Suite tools. (2 years+)
  
– Experience working in a fast-paced role, to problem solve/troubleshoot, while working independently and in a team environments. (2 years+)
  
– Relevant experience in a role similar to this. Experience must be applicable to this role. (2 years+)
  
– Experience working with clients/stakeholders to identify, gather, document, and analyze business data and process requirements. (2 years+)

**DESIRABLE / NICE TO HAVE SKILLS**

– Relevant post-secondary education in the area of office administration. Acceptable education includes degrees, diplomas and certificates. (Yes or No)
  
– Experience with Information Governance, or records management and information management. (2 years+)
  
– Experience with information management concepts, privacy, and security issues relating to ATIA (Access to Information Act) and POPA (Protection of Privacy Act) – previously known as FOIP. (2 years+)
  
– Experience working directly within the Government of Alberta, 1GX (SAP), or a comparable Canadian public-sector ERP environment. (2 years+)
  
– Experience working with workers compensation systems (i.e. WCB). (2 years+)

**NOT FOR YOU?**

Check out our other opportunities at https://tri-global.com or follow us on LinkedIn. We thank all candidates in advance. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

**Area Supervisor – Power & Utilities**

. As the technical subject matter expert, they are expected to guide, train, and lead the Power & Utilities operations team members, support maintenance planning and execution, and liaise with technical, maintenance, and turnaround departments. The successful candidate will serve as a key operational leader, ensuring safe, reliable, and efficient utility operations while supporting commissioning, startup, and long-term plant performance. At Air Products we foster a culture of inclusion where every voice is heard, and everyone feels they belong and matter. Additionally, we offer competitive pay and phenomenal benefits for our employees. Check out some of our benefits below!

* Defined Contribution Pension Plan (DCPP) at 4% of base pay

* Ensure environmental compliance and support sustainability objectives.
* Train, assess, mentor, and develop a team of operators and technicians.
* Develop site talent through coaching, training, progression planning, and succession development.
* Foster a culture of continuous improvement, operational excellence, and employee involvement.

**Physical Requirements**

**About Us**
------------

MacEwan University is where caring faculty help people connect their passions to their future paths. Located in the heart of Edmonton's diverse and dynamic downtown community, and on the traditional lands of Treaty 6 First Nations and homelands of the Métis people, MacEwan is known for exceptional undergraduate learning. With its dedication to teaching excellence, informed by scholarly research, innovation, and creative activity, MacEwan provides an exceptional collaborative and supportive learning environment with a commitment to human rights, environmental sustainability, and opportunities for community engagement. We are committed to creating an equitable, diverse, inclusive, and welcoming community for all peoples, cultures, and identities.
  
  
Our comprehensive undergraduate university offers 55 programs to more than 21,000 full- and part-time students in business, communications, community and human services, design, fine and performing arts, health, humanities, natural science, nursing, public safety, and social science. Through a wide array of experiential learning opportunities, and strategic relationships in the community, we partner with others to produce graduates of stature. Along with a robust grounding in their chosen disciplines, MacEwan students are given durable life skills that prepare them to take on the world.

**Opportunity**
---------------

MacEwan University is seeking a Supervisor, Student Recruitment – International for a full-time continuing opportunity with the Office of the University Registrar (OUR).

Reporting to the Manager, Student Recruitment, you will be accountable for the planning, implementation, and evaluation of MacEwan University’s student recruitment activities focused on international markets. You will play a key role in the development of strategies and initiatives to strengthen the university’s brand, attract and recruit future students, and achieve application and new student enrolment goals set out in the University's strategic enrolment management plan. You will also provide day-to-day operational leadership and supervision of the international student recruitment team and oversee the educational agent portfolios.

Key responsibilities include:

* Assisting the Manager in the development of short and long-term international recruitment strategies, including targeting by country, program and agent for the beginning of fall and winter terms;
* Ensuring that recruitment goals set by senior administration are achieved;
* Measuring effectiveness of recruitment activities by developing and maintaining a system to capture and analyze statistical and database information by country, program, and educational agent in conjunction with Institutional Analysis & Planning (IAP);
* Supervising and guiding a team of international student recruiters; by assigning, distributing, reviewing, organizing, coordinating, and prioritizing workloads;
* Monitoring assignments, deadlines, and ensuring goals and objectives are met in alignment with quality and quantity standards;
* Serving as a point of contact, reference and escalation for the team;
* Working with international student recruiters to discuss problems, providing solutions and advice, and removing barriers to success through active problem-solving, based on knowledge of established processes, practices and standards;
* Undertaking recruitment activities in select countries as required;
* Collaborating with educational agents and high schools to promote MacEwan University as a choice destination; and
* Conducting appropriate post trip follow up with educational agents and schools ensuring ongoing communication within the recruitment process.

#### **Skills**

You will have:

* Excellent intercultural competence, while demonstrating a solid cross-cultural understanding including knowledge and awareness of cultural norms and sensitivities, business etiquette, traditions, and diplomatic protocol;
* The ability to practice sound judgment and professionalism when working with internal and external partners and stakeholders of diverse backgrounds;
* The ability to demonstrate a thorough understanding of diverse cultural context and global perspectives;
* High-level communication skills, including excellent written and oral skills, as well as social media literacy and fluency;
* Dynamic and energetic public speaking abilities to effectively promote the university brand and concisely explain program offerings, admission pathways, requirements, and processes;
* The ability to build positive, productive relationships with diverse groups of people, including academic leaders, managers, faculty, staff, future students, and other university stakeholders;
* Effective team leadership and management skills with the ability to provide direction and subsequently plan, organize, delegate, and evaluate work in collaboration with others;
* The ability to effectively motivate staff and establish a high-performance team and culture to achieve required goals and outcomes;
* The ability to perform complex tasks using Microsoft Office Suite customer relationship management software, and student information systems such as PeopleSoft and Business Intelligence;
* Proven critical thinking, conflict resolution, and collaborative decision-making skills;
* The ability to collect and analyze applicant and student data to inform evidence-based decisions and evaluate effectiveness of ongoing student recruitment activities and new initiatives with a student experience orientation;
* Effective problem-solving skills and the ability to make decisions independently in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment;
* An understanding of International secondary and post-secondary systems with the ability to understand, interpret and apply University policies and procedures, admission requirements, and strategic enrolment management objectives and goals;
* Knowledge of best practices, initiatives, current research and thinking in student enrolment management, and the ability to assess their relevance and apply within the MacEwan University context;
* The ability to deal competently and discreetly with sensitive issues;
* Flexibility to manage multiple tasks and priorities, including the ability to deal with ambiguity and competing demands; and
* A proven ability to manage special events and projects.

#### **Qualifications**

* A minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree in International Relations, Education, Business, Administration, or related field.
* A minimum of 4 years of international recruitment experience and experience with supervising staff.
* Experience working with students and faculty, as well as developing successful relationships and stakeholder management.
* A minimum of 2 years of experience working in a post-secondary environment would be considered an asset.

* Experience studying or living abroad, and proficiency in a language other than English would be considered assets.

* RCIC or RISIA certification would be considered an asset.
* An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

#### **Position Requirements**

* This position is on campus only.
* The ability, willingness, and flexibility to travel and work irregular hours.
* Must have valid drivers' license and access to a reliable vehicle.
* Must have valid Canadian passport with the ability to travel internationally and navigate different systems while travelling internationally.

#### **Benefits**

When you become part of the MacEwan University team, you will enjoy a competitive salary. Our total compensation package includes:

* Competitive base pay
* Generous vacation time
* Secure pension plan
* Flexible benefits package
* Continuous learning culture
* Opportunities for career growth

**How to Apply**
----------------

To apply, please head to our MacEwan University Opportunities Page, select the job opportunity and click Apply Now. If you require assistance, please contact us at careers@macewan.ca.

If you are experiencing technical difficulties when submitting your application, please try submitting through a different browser (i.e., Safari, Firefox, Chrome, etc.). If the issue persists, please send a screenshot of the error message to careers@macewan.ca so we can assist and ensure your application is received.

This position is included under the MacEwan Staff Union Collective Agreement.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.
